key_insight: Increasing the O₂/C₂H₂ ratio to 1.2 produced denser Ni–Cr–B–Si coatings with lower porosity and roughness and higher adhesion, while peak microhardness occurred at 1.1.
engineering_relevance: Gas-ratio control offers a practical way to tailor flame-sprayed coating quality on AISI 321 steel, with different settings favoring hardness versus adhesion and density.
method: Deposited Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings using a Metal Coat 6PM-II at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2.
Monitored spraying parameters with an Accuraspray 4.0 diagnostic system.
Characterized microstructure, porosity, microhardness, surface roughness, and adhesion strength.
evidence_signal: Across the tested ratio range, porosity decreased from 1.97 ± 0.13% to 0.90 ± 0.09%, roughness from 4.70 ± 0.09 to 2.99 ± 0.11 μm, and adhesion increased from 22.14 ± 4.3 to 35.02 ± 3.9 MPa; peak average microhardness was 1051.7 HV at 1.1.
watch_item: The abstract does not report absolute spray temperatures or service-life testing, so gas-ratio optimization should not be treated as a validated temperature window or durability guarantee.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
